unit_title: Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge - Grammar Focus (Direct and Indirect/Reported Speech)
content: Unit 4: Grammar Focus - Direct and Indirect (Reported) Speech (Communicative English Skills II - EnLa102) ========================================= 1. CORE CONCEPTS AND FUNDAMENTALS OF REPORTED SPEECH ========================================= What is Direct and Indirect (Reported) Speech? In English grammar, we use two main ways to report what someone else said: Direct Speech (ቀጥተኛ ንግግር) and Indirect / Reported Speech (እርምጃ/ዘገባዊ ንግግር)። A. Direct Speech (ቀጥተኛ ንግግር): Direct speech quotes the exact words spoken by a person inside quotation marks ("..."). Example: Ayele said, "I've been asked to take you to her." - Exact Spoken Words: "I've been asked to take you to her." - Reporting Verb: said B. Indirect / Reported Speech (ዘገባዊ ንግግር): Reported speech conveys the meaning of what someone said without using exact words by removing quotation marks, shifting pronouns, backshifting tenses, and adjusting time/place adverbs. Example: Ayele explained that he had been asked to take her to her. - Reporting Verb + Conjunction: explained that - Pronoun Shift: I've → he had - Tense Shift: Present Perfect Passive → Past Perfect Passive Why Do We Use Reported Speech? 1. To summarize academic and field conversations: Avoids repetitive quotation marks in essays and reports. 2. To report events and research findings: Allows objective narration of interviews, history, and indigenous knowledge discussions. 3. To maintain grammatical consistency: Keeps the narration in the past time frame when reporting past conversations. THE THREE GOLDEN SHIFTS IN REPORTED SPEECH: When transforming Direct Speech to Indirect Speech in past reporting contexts, always apply: 1. Tense Shift (Backshifting): Move the main verb one step back into the past. 2. Pronoun Shift: Change pronouns to reflect the reporter's perspective (I → he/she, we → they, my → his/her). 3. Time and Place Shift: Update adverbs of time and place (now → then, today → that day, here → there). ========================================= 2. COMPREHENSIVE GRAMMAR MATRIX, RULES & CLUES ========================================= A. Complete Tense Backshifting Matrix • Simple Present → Simple Past Active Direct: "I love Ireland," Tedla said. Active Indirect: Tedla said that he loved Ireland. (ቅያሬ፦ Simple Present 'love' ወደ Simple Past 'loved' ተቀይሯል።) • Present Continuous → Past Continuous Active Direct: "What are you doing here, Tedla?" Betru asked. Active Indirect: Betru asked Tedla what he was doing there. (ቅያሬ፦ Present Continuous 'are doing' ወደ Past Continuous 'was doing' ተቀይሯል።) • Present Perfect → Past Perfect Active Direct: "I haven't seen you since June," Betru said. Active Indirect: Betru said that he hadn't seen him since June. (ቅያሬ፦ Present Perfect 'haven't seen' ወደ Past Perfect 'hadn't seen' ተቀይሯል።) • Simple Past → Past Perfect Active Direct: "Did you go to Shambu?" Betru asked. Active Indirect: Betru asked if he had gone to Shambu. (ቅያሬ፦ Simple Past 'did go' ወደ Past Perfect 'had gone' ተቀይሯል።) • Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous Active Direct: "We were discussing local traditions," she said. Active Indirect: She said that they had been discussing local traditions. • Future (Will) → Conditional (Would) Active Direct: "I'll be there at eight," Betru said. Active Indirect: Betru said that he would be there at eight. B. Modal Verbs Shift & Rules - Can → Could ("I can show you pictures" → He said he could show him pictures) - May → Might ("May I help you?" → The porter asked if he might help me) - Must → Had to / Must ("I must arrange things" → Betru said he had to arrange things) - Shall → Should / Would (depending on recommendation or future prediction) - Might / Could / Should / Would / Ought to → Remain Unchanged C. Time and Place Adverb Transformations (Clue List) - now → then / at that moment - today → that day - tonight → that night - tomorrow → the next day / the following day - yesterday → the day before / the previous day - here → there - this / these → that / those - ago → before - next week → the following week ========================================= 3. ADVANCED GRAMMAR RULES, EXAM TRICKS & PITFALL CASES ========================================= Pitfall Case 1: Reporting Verb in Simple Present Tense (NO Backshifting!) If the reporting verb is in the Present Tense (e.g., says, tells, asks, claims), do NOT change the verb tense inside the reported sentence! Only change pronouns. - Direct: He says, "I love studying indigenous knowledge." - Incorrect: He says that he loved studying indigenous knowledge. - Correct: He says that he loves studying indigenous knowledge. Pitfall Case 2: Universal Truths and General Facts (NO Backshifting!) When reporting scientific facts, general truths, or permanent states, the tense remains unchanged even if the reporting verb is in the past tense. - Direct: The teacher said, "Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius." - Correct: The teacher said that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Pitfall Case 3: 'Say' vs 'Tell' Usage - Tell must always be followed by a personal object (e.g., told me, told Betru). - Say is NOT followed by a personal object unless 'to' is added (e.g., said that..., said to me). - Incorrect: Betru told that he was free. - Correct: Betru said that he was free / Betru told me that he was free. Pitfall Case 4: Reporting Questions - Word Order & 'If/Whether' Shift When transforming questions into reported speech: 1. Change question word order to statement word order (Subject + Verb). 2. Omit auxiliary verbs like do, does, did. 3. For Yes/No questions, insert if or whether. - Direct: "Do you want it?" Joe asked me. - Incorrect: Joe asked me did I want it. - Correct: Joe asked me if I wanted it. Pitfall Case 5: Reporting Imperatives (Commands, Requests, Advice) Imperatives use To + Verb 1 (Affirmative) or Not to + Verb 1 (Negative). - Direct: "Don't joke," Mum said to Mark. - Incorrect: Mum told Mark to not joke. - Correct: Mum told Mark not to joke. - Direct: "Try moving it," Rahel said. - Correct: Rahel advised her to try moving it. ========================================= 4. PRACTICE EXAM PITFALL QUESTIONS & DETAILED ANALYSIS ========================================= Question 1: Direct Speech: "Where did you live?" They wanted to know ________. A. where did I live B. where I had lived C. where I lived D. where had I lived Correct Answer: B. where I had lived Analysis / Rationale: Simple Past question ("did you live") shifts to Past Perfect ("had lived") in reported speech, and the word order changes from question to statement (Subject 'I' before verb 'had lived'). Question 2: Select the CORRECT indirect form of: Tedla said, "I can show you some pictures tomorrow." A. Tedla said that he could show me some pictures tomorrow. B. Tedla said that he can show me some pictures the next day. C. Tedla said that he could show me some pictures the following day. D. Tedla said that he will show me some pictures the following day. Correct Answer: C. Tedla said that he could show me some pictures the following day. Analysis / Rationale: 'can' backshifts to 'could', and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the following day'. Question 3: Identify the grammatically INCORRECT reported sentence: A. My friend asked me where I was. B. He requested me to not make noise during the lecture. C. She asked if I had set my alarm clock. D. The lecturer stated that light travels faster than sound. Correct Answer: B. He requested me to not make noise during the lecture. Analysis / Rationale: Negative imperative reported speech requires 'not to + V1' ("not to make noise"), NOT 'to not make noise'. Question 4: Mark: "Dad says that he ________ his voice." A. lost B. had lost C. has lost D. losing Correct Answer: C. has lost Analysis / Rationale: Because the reporting verb 'says' is in the present tense, the tense inside the reported clause remains in the present perfect ('has lost') without backshifting. Question 5: Choose the sentence that contains a reporting verb error: A. Betru told me that he was free that night. B. Betru told that he was free that night. C. Betru said that he was free that night. D. Betru said to me that he was free that night. Correct Answer: B. Betru told that he was free that night. Analysis / Rationale: The verb 'tell' requires an indirect personal object (e.g., 'told me'). Using 'told that' without an object is grammatically incorrect. Question 6: Direct Speech: "Are you doing anything tomorrow?" Tedla asked Betru. A. Tedla asked Betru if he was doing anything the next day. B. Tedla asked Betru was he doing anything tomorrow. C. Tedla asked Betru if he is doing anything the next day. D. Tedla asked Betru what he was doing the next day. Correct Answer: A. Tedla asked Betru if he was doing anything the next day. Analysis / Rationale: Yes/No continuous question uses 'if' + Past Continuous ('was doing') + time adverb shift ('the next day'). Question 7: Choose the sentence that correctly converts: "We must protect indigenous knowledge," Birhane stated. A. Birhane stated that they must protect indigenous knowledge. B. Birhane stated that they had to protect indigenous knowledge. C. Birhane stated that we must protect indigenous knowledge. D. Both A and B are correct. Correct Answer: D. Both A and B are correct. Analysis / Rationale: 'Must' in reported speech can either change to 'had to' or remain 'must' when expressing a general moral duty/obligation.
